source_text: Ex quo iam spiritalibus animis patere confido nullam naturam deo esse posse contrariam. si enim ille est et de solo deo proprie dici potest hoc uerbum — quod enim uere est, incommutabiliter manet, quoniam quod mutatur, fuit aliquid, quod iam non est, et erit, quod nondum est — nihil habet deus contrarium. si enim quaereretur a nobis, quid sit albo contrarium, responderemus nigrum; si quaereretur, quid sit calido contrarium, responderemus frigidum; si quaereretur, quid sit ueloci contrarium, responderemus tardum, et quaecumque similia. cum autem quaeritur, quid sit contrarium ei quod est, recte respondetur: quod non est.
thought_title: Nothing is contrary to God, who alone truly is
orientation: Augustine has just cited God's self-revelation to Moses as 'I am who I am' and now draws the conclusion that no nature can be contrary to God.
pass_a_gloss: From which now [to] spiritual souls to be open I am confident no nature to God to be able to be contrary. if for he is and of [the] only God properly can be said this word — [that] which for truly is, unchangeably remains, since [that] which is changed, was something, which now not is, and will be, which not yet is — nothing has God contrary. if for it were asked from us, what might be to white contrary, we would answer black; if it were asked, what might be to hot contrary, we would answer cold; if it were asked, what might be to swift contrary, we would answer slow, and whatever similar [things]. when however it is asked, what might be contrary to that which is, rightly it is answered: that which not is.

choices.why: Keeps the adjective-noun pairing of the source; 'spiritual' renders spiritalibus and 'souls' renders animis, matching the glossary's sense of anima as soul.
Standard rendering for natura in philosophical context; Augustine is speaking of any kind of existing thing.
Adverb plus verb preserves the source's emphasis on the manner of remaining; 'unchangeably' matches incommutabiliter.
Literal rendering of the relative clause; preserves the philosophical force of non-being as the contrary of being.
Renders the impersonal passive with the adverb recte as an adjectival phrase, keeping the evaluative force.

pass_b_english: From this point I am confident it is now evident to spiritual souls that no nature can be contrary to God. For if he is—and this word can properly be said of God alone, since what truly is remains unchangeably, because what is changed was something that no longer is, and will be something that is not yet—then God has nothing contrary to him. If someone asked us what is contrary to white, we would answer: black. If someone asked what is contrary to hot, we would answer: cold. If someone asked what is contrary to fast, we would answer: slow, and so on with similar cases. But when the question is what is contrary to that which is, the right answer is: that which is not.

last_rejected.quote: since what truly is remains unchangeably
last_rejected.source_quote: quod enim uere est, incommutabiliter manet
last_rejected.why: 'remains unchangeably' is adverbial; 'unchangeably' is awkward and slightly obscures that the subject remains, not the manner.
last_rejected.fix: since what truly is remains unchangeable
last_rejected.ruling: 'incommutabiliter manet' = 'remains unchangeably'; adverb correctly modifies verb. Awkwardness is stylistic, not a meaning change.
